cards.summary: Sitting rabbit in profile facing right: two tall ears up, a round head with a short muzzle, a big rounded haunch and the forepaws tucked in front. Solid black, about 0.85 to 1.
avoid: no eye, tail or whisker detail: it reads by outline only
ears are the only thin parts; they blunt when stroked
cards.applies_to: shape layer / vector path: drawn with the Custom Shape tool as a Shape layer (Fill and Stroke stay editable, it scales without loss); Path mode gives an outline for clipping or vector masks, Pixels mode paints it into a pixel layer. It is not an effect and does nothing to photo content by itself.
cards.how_to_apply: By script (the route PGD used for the thumbnail): load <Photoshop 2026 install folder>/Required/Legacy Shapes and More.csh as custom shapes, then Action Manager make on a contentLayer whose shape is a customShape descriptor with this name, this ID ('5d98b129-d6c6-11d5-a761-e18a5aa4c756': the .csh file stores it as $5d98b129-d6c6-11d5-a761-e18a5aa4c756, the PGD renderer passes it without the $) and Top/Left/Btom/Rght pixel bounds plus a solidColorLayer fill; the library must be loaded first. In the interface the Custom Shape tool (U, Shift+U cycles the shape tools) should list it in the shape picker (options bar) or Shapes panel under the group path 'Legacy Shapes and More/All Legacy Default Shapes/Animals' as stored in the .csh file; PGD did not drive the picker, so those clicks are inferred, not observed. Drag on the canvas (Shift keeps proportions) and set Fill / Stroke in the options bar.
cards.notes: PGD thumbnail: applied in Photoshop as a custom shape layer (by name and ID), filled near-black on white and fitted to the shape's own aspect ratio. Shapes are single-colour paths: white areas inside the black are holes (cut-outs) in the path, not white paint. Pixel check of the 320 px thumbnail: no fully enclosed white holes; white inside the outline, where present, is open to the outside (a cut channel or gap).

verified.note: Sitting rabbit facing right with two tall ears, round head, big haunch and forepaws in front.
